baseline: ee0e76be (Tigris pool) on the 3bf6bb2e matched-weather field code
known: Archived matched-weather capture cases use a pre-sowing August-October capture window. Nile capture coverage: Hargreaves 70.827 / 81.521%, Penman-Monteith 53.930 / 67.850% (5-bin / 4-bin fractional). Mesopotamia with the Tigris pool: 2.524 / 2.604% and 0.674 / 0.728%, identical to Euphrates-only; 10.2 of 11.05 km3 of flood water flows past because both rivers peak in March-July. Monthly source excess is known for all three gauges. No output with any other capture window has been computed.
question: Does letting fields draw river water while the crop stands (canal-style refilling of the root zone) change the Nile gain or inflate Mesopotamia, with the river source rule and everything else unchanged?

windows.pre_sowing: Archived rule: capture during August-October (flood day to sowing day), ponds permitted then.
windows.in_crop: Capture only during the supplied crop window. Ponds are not permitted on a standing crop (existing rule), so a request refills the soil up to capacity at the 20 mm/day infiltration limit.

cases: Nile (Aswan) and Mesopotamia (Hit + Mosul pooled source); matched meteorology; Hargreaves and Penman-Monteith; both supplied calendars; capture on. pre_sowing is recomputed and must reproduce the archived arrays exactly (8 controls: Nile from 3bf6bb2e, Mesopotamia from ee0e76be). in_crop and both are new: 16 cases.
fixed: River source = positive excess above the annual mean of the mean monthly flow (no base-flow diversion); one ideal pool per region; barley, 1.5 m roots, bare 0.15, pond 200 mm, efficiency 1; all candidates consume water; eligibility from matched temperature. No window is chosen by results.
test_framing: Report Nile gain and Mesopotamia change for each window. A window that raises Mesopotamia while leaving the Nile unchanged would be the inflation the planned test guards against; a window that helps neither shows the source rule, not timing, as the next limit.
stated_limits: Excess-only source means winter base flow cannot be diverted; Mosul understates the lower Tigris; root coverage is a water diagnostic, not grain or area.
review: Independent scalar reference (the reviewed one, with the capture mask separated from the pond mask by a declared substitution); annual field stocks/fluxes, monthly basin ledgers, daily stocks for all 24 runs; fresh byte replay; protected outputs unchanged.
